title: Variant rotation schedule and staged commit framework for hosted model catalog
creator: Morgan Reyes
description: Summary: Define a repeatable schedule and staged-commit framework for rotating hosted model variants (quantized, fp16, small/medium/large) across the Hosted API catalog. The goal is to enable predictable quarter-by-quarter model upgrades while protecting latency and cost SLOs and providing clear rollback paths. This ticket covers cadence, canary sizing, metric gates, and runbook hooks tied to the Console and alerting dashboards. Context: As we increase cadence for model variant updates, product teams need a low-friction way to opt into rotations and a platform-level safety net for failures. Current model rotations are ad hoc, causing surprise latency regressions and uneven rollout velocity across customers. Deliverables: a templated schedule, staged-commit checklist, gating metrics, playbook snippets for Console rollouts, and a verification dashboard query set.
success_metrics: No customer-facing latency regressions >10% in production during rotation windows
Canary failure detection and automatic rollback within 15 minutes for 95% of incidents
Average time from scheduled rotation to full graduation reduced from 7 days to 48 hours
Clear owner sign-off recorded in Console for 100% of rotations in Q3
milestones: M1: Define rotation cadence and stakeholder signoff (by 2026-04-01)
M2: Implement staged-commit checklist as Console template (by 2026-04-20)
M3: Canary telemetry queries and dashboards live (by 2026-05-05)
M4: Run two internal test rotations (canary+pilot) and validate rollback (by 2026-05-20)
M5: Publish public docs and runbook, enable opt-in scheduling for customers (by 2026-06-10)
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Preflight - confirm model artifact signatures, compatibility matrix, and capacity plan
Phase 1: Canary - 0.5% of tokens, 30 minute steady-state observation, metric gates applied (latency P90, error-rate, perplexity proxy)
Phase 2: Pilot - 5% of tokens across 3 representative customers for 24 hours
Phase 3: Gradual ramp - 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 24-48 hour windows with automated gating and manual overrides
Phase 4: Post-rollover validation - 72 hour monitoring window with automated regression alert suppression whitelist for known anomalies
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Latency regressions due to unforeseen kernel scheduling behavior. Mitigation: require perf microbench on production-like infra and include fallback variant pinned at previous runtime-1.x for instant routing fallback.
Risk: Cost spike from inadvertent traffic routing to higher-cost variants. Mitigation: add cost SLO gate and limit canary capacity; pre-authorize burst budget and monitor token-level cost in Console.
Risk: Insufficient observability for semantic regressions. Mitigation: tie rotation gating to a small prompt-synth corpus and automated evaluation (quality regression >= threshold triggers rollback).
Risk: Cross-region inconsistency during rolling updates. Mitigation: enforce region-by-region commit windows and require cross-region parity checks before wide rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Rotation cadence and written timeline approved by Product, Runtime, and DevEx leads

A5: Public-facing documentation and customer opt-in controls published to docs.redwood.ai
